To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

ipsenol (a synomone of Ipslattidens) and verbenone (a synom one of Dendroctonusponderosae) can be used together to reduce the number of attacks by Ipspini (Coleoptera:Scolytidae) on felled and standing trees.
the synomones ipsenol and/or verbenone, released at 5 m centres in 4 × 4 grids, reduced attack density of Ipspini by 74% in standing pines.

the capture of the pine engraver in traps baited with ipdienol was significantly reduced by the release of verbenone or ipsenol from devices within the traps, that the release of verbeenol and ipsenol together from devices on felled trees reduced the attack density on the trees by 98.8%, and that the release of these compounds together from devices on standing trees reduced the attack by 74.1%.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the use of semiochemicals to protect trees from bark beetle attack.
the development of an antiaggregant pheromone formulation that can be applied to the trunk of a tree, or to a tree stump, to deter the colonization of the tree by bark beetles.
the development of a new generation of semiochemicals for use in the management of bark beetles and their associated pathogens.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the synomones verbenone and ipdenol are effective at reducing the number of logs and trees attacked by the pine engravers.
the synomones of two species of bark beetles deter attack by a third species.
the antiaggregant effects of verbenone and ipdienol are not additive but that the combination of the two compounds results in a greater reduction in attack density than either compound alone.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the use of verbenone and/or ipsenol to deter attack by pine engravers is an important new management tool for forest health.
verbenone and verbenone plus ipdienol are effective antiaggregants for the mountain pine beetle.

the use of verbenone and/or ipsenol as antiaggregants for the control of bark beetles is a practical and environmentally acceptable alternative to the use of pheromone-based attractants and toxicants.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we can use pheromones to protect our pine trees from the pine engravers, which is a very important insect pest.
verbenone and/or ipsenol are very effective in reducing Ipspini attack on both felled and standing trees.
the antiaggregant pheromone blend of verbenone and ipdienol is effective in reducing Ips pini attack in both felled trees and standing pines.
